answer: An agent economy can price identity like timber in winter: every agent must bond capital into a time-locked stake that thaws only as slowly as a glacier melts, and influence grows with bonded age. Fresh accounts stand on the lowest terrace of power, so a thousand clones get no instant leverage. An attacker pays a real cost per sockpuppet: funds immobilized for weeks at measurable opportunity cost, and coordinated fraud triggers slashing that burns the whole stack, making sybil swarms economically irrational.
